reasons: Candidate wraps the monotonic sum in rate(), but the Datadog query has no rate function and reads the raw count, so the quantity and unit differ (rows/s vs rows).

Datadog groups by {db}; the candidate has no by-clause, so the series are collapsed into one global average instead of one series per database. Grouping should use the observed label postgresql_database_name.

Template variables are dropped: $db (prefix db) should become postgresql_database_name=~"$db" and $host (prefix host) should become host_name=~"$host", which are observed labels. The candidate applies no matchers, so the series set differs.
The aggregation avg() over all series differs from the per-db average in the Datadog request.
Outcome translated is correct because the metric mapping exists (postgresql.tup_updated measures rows updated), so only the PromQL needs fixing.
